questions: Did the drooping of your eyelid start suddenly?
Are you experiencing any pain in your head, face, or neck?
Have you noticed that the right side of your face is sweating less than the left?
Have you had any recent trauma or injury to your head or neck?
orders: Cocaine 4% or 10% eye drop test (applied to both eyes to confirm Horner's syndrome)
Apraclonidine 1% eye drop test (alternative confirmation if cocaine unavailable)
MRI of the brain and pituitary region with dedicated thin-cut sequences through the cavernous sinus
MRI of the neck with contrast to evaluate the sympathetic chain
results: 1. Cocaine 4% or 10% eye drop test (applied to both eyes to confirm Horner's syndrome)
2. Apraclonidine 1% eye drop test (alternative confirmation if cocaine unavailable)

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS:
Right Horner's syndrome secondary to Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C, cerebellar type)

Alternatives:
1. Spinocerebellar ataxia with Horner's syndrome
2. Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration with Horner's syndrome
3. Isolated right ptosis (age-related levator dehiscence) with coincidental cerebellar atrophy
